title: Rhubarb Curd
subtitle: Pale pink curd with rhubarb's distinct sharpness
excerpt: Rhubarb curd uses stewed and strained rhubarb juice as the acid base instead of citrus. The colour is a soft blush pink. Makes two small jars and keeps 3 weeks in the fridge.
sourceNotes: Pam Corbin, Preserves. Rhubarb juice replaces citrus as the acid; the oxalic acid in rhubarb helps thicken the egg base but it sets softer than lemon curd.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge.

glossaryTerms.definition: A heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of barely simmering water, used for delicate heat-sensitive mixtures like curd and custard.

content.text: Rhubarb curd uses the juice extracted from stewed rhubarb as the acid base,  it has a specific, tangy sharpness that is distinctly its own. The finished curd is a pale blush pink and softer-set than lemon curd, since rhubarb is less acidic than citrus. Makes about two 200 g jars.

Put the rhubarb in a saucepan with 2 tablespoons of water. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the rhubarb completely collapses and releases its juice, about 8 to 10 minutes. Tip into a fine sieve set over a bowl and press firmly to extract as much juice as possible. You need about 100 ml. Discard the pulp.
Put the rhubarb juice, lemon juice, sugar, and butter in a heatproof

a pan of barely simmering water. Stir until the butter melts and sugar dissolves. Add the beaten eggs and stir constantly for 15 to 20 minutes until the curd thickens enough to coat a spoon. The water must stay at a gentle simmer.
Strain through a fine sieve into hot sterilised jars. Seal and cool. Rhubarb curd thickens more on cooling than lemon curd does.

items.symptom: Curd is very pale or almost white
items.cause: Green rhubarb has less pigment than forced (pink) rhubarb.
items.fix: Use forced rhubarb, the bright pink stems from Yorkshire forcing sheds give a much more vivid colour. Field rhubarb will always give a paler result.

items.symptom: Curd is too thin even when cold
items.cause: Rhubarb is less acidic than lemon, so the set is softer.
items.fix: Add a second tablespoon of lemon juice or use an extra egg yolk. Rhubarb curd will never be as firm as lemon.

items.cause: Rhubarb fibres made it through the sieve.
items.fix: Press more firmly through a fine-mesh sieve, or pass through twice.

items.cause: Not enough rhubarb flavour after cooking and diluting with butter and sugar.
items.fix: Reduce the butter to 60 g and the sugar to 130 g to let the rhubarb character come through more clearly.

content.text: Refrigerate immediately. Use within 3 weeks. Freezes for up to 3 months.
